subject: Re: Performance remedies & termination language - ND-3491
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@nimbushealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial request: performance remedies & termination rights (ND-3491)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks promising and aligns well with our integration roadmap. Before we can proceed to final signatures, our legal and risk teams asked us to get clarity and firm commitments around performance and termination. Given that NimbusHealth is a regulated provider, availability and tail latency directly map to patient-facing risk; credits alone do not sufficiently compensate for business and regulatory exposure.

Specifically, we are requesting the following in the MSAs/SOW:
- Fee-at-risk: an escrow equal to six (6) months of monthly recurring fees held for the term as security for recurring severe outages.
- Liquidated damages: in the event of a P1 incident that produces sustained degraded latency (>500ms median p95 across affected routes) for more than 4 hours, LDs equal to 100% of that month’s fees for the affected routes.
- Termination rights: immediate right to terminate for convenience with 30 days’ notice after 3 separate P1 incidents within any rolling 60-day window.

We appreciate that these asks are strong. To be explicit: Nimbus is unwilling to proceed to procurement without either these remedies or a clearly equivalent alternative that gives us the same level of financial and exit protection. Please share any proposed redline language as soon as you can and identify internal owners for negotiation.

I’ve attached our procurement checklist and the SLA summary the compliance team will use to sign off.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Wu
VP, Vendor Risk & Compliance
NimbusHealth
Attachments: Nimbus_SLA_Request_20261118.pdf, Nimbus_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial request: performance remedies & termination rights (ND-3491)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the note and for sharing the checklist. I appreciate the compliance team's clarity; I understand why the remedies you propose feel necessary given the regulatory exposure.

High-level response while we pull legal input:
- We cannot accept an open-ended 100% monthly LD for each P1 as drafted. That would be disproportionate and would jeopardize our ability to operate predictably.
- We can propose a staged alternative: an escrow equal to three (3) months of committed fees (escrowed at signing) plus an escalating buyout schedule tied to repeated, uncured P1s (for example: first sustained P1 -> enhanced credits + mandatory root-cause plan; second within window -> additional reserved fees applied toward remediation; third -> negotiated buyout option).
- We are willing to include a termination right tied to repeat severe degradation, but we need a cure window (we typically see 14–30 day cure periods) and objective severity definitions (e.g., p95 tail sustained over 4 hours, verified by both sides’ telemetry).

I’ve looped in Aditya (commercial) and Marissa (legal) to propose language and quantify the financial trade-offs so we can present a single compromise. If Nimbus can accept a dedicated capacity or pinned model variant for the highest-risk routes, that also reduces the need for large escrow.

Next steps: Marissa will share a redline by tomorrow EOD. Aditya and I can model the escrow/buyout economics in a short note for your procurement team.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood proposed redlines — performance remedies (ND-3491)

Elaine / Lauren / team,

Attached is Redwood_SLA_Redline_v1.docx with tracked changes (excerpted below). High-level points for Nimbus to consider:

1) Escrow and fee-at-risk
- Counterproposal: escrow equal to three (3) months of committed recurring fees, deposited at signing and released pro rata over the first 12 months unless drawn for validated SLA credit payments or remediation costs.
- Rationale: provides meaningful security while aligning with our underwriting limits.

2) Liquidated damages and caps
- We propose applying an SLA credit regime that scales with severity and duration; a limited LD only if the service provider is found to have materially breached SLAs and the breach is not remedied within a specified cure period. Any LDs would be subject to an aggregate cap equal to the total fees paid in the prior 12 months.
- Rationale: protects both parties vs open-ended exposure.

3) Termination triggers and cure periods
- Proposed termination: Nimbus may terminate for cause if there are three (3) verified P1 incidents within a rolling 90-day window and Redwood fails to remedy the root cause within thirty (30) days after the third incident’s RCA and remediation plan are mutually agreed.
- We added explicit verification steps, joint telemetry reviews, and escalation to a VP-level remediation committee prior to termination.

4) Objective definitions and exclusions
- We included objective metrics (p95 latency, error-rate delta, affected route list). Exclusions for force majeure, planned maintenance, and customer-side misconfigurations are explicit.

5) Operational mitigations
- Offer: Redwood will commit to a pilot of dedicated capacity for the highest-risk routes for the first 6 months of live production at a discounted uplift — this materially reduces the probability of repeated P1s.

We believe this package balances Nimbus’s need for protection and Redwood’s requirement to keep exposure insurable and predictable. Please review the attached docx; we can schedule a call Friday afternoon to walk through the redline.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Deputy General Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Redline_v1.docx
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@nimbushealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redlines — performance remedies (ND-3491)

Lauren / Marissa — thank you for the quick review and the redline. We appreciate the dedicated-capacity pilot offer and the move toward objective definitions. A few points from procurement and risk that are hard lines for us:

1) Escrow: three months is better but insufficient given the regulatory penalties we might face. Nimbus must retain the option to require an escrow equal to six months (to be drawn only for validated, repeated severe incidents). Without the option we cannot justify the downstream risk to our board.

2) Termination window: 90 days is long in our view — repeated outages over 90 days would already have caused material harm. We can accept verification steps but require that the rolling window be 60 days, not 90.

3) Aggregate cap: capping LDs to the prior 12 months’ fees hides tail risk. We propose a tiered cap: up to 12 months fees for operational incidents, up to 18 months for incidents that lead to regulatory fines against Nimbus.

We are prepared to escalate to our CIO and Chief Legal Officer if necessary, but we’d prefer to resolve with Redwood commercial and legal this week. If Redwood can accept the 6-month optional escrow + 60-day rolling window + tiered cap, we can move to signature immediately and start SOW work.

Please indicate whether these are acceptable or whether we should schedule an escalation call. Procurement has attached their final checklist with the redline margins.

Thanks,
Elaine
